item.title: 17-year-old Maiwiriwiri excited to represent Fiji at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 17-year-old Anastasia Maiwiriwiri of Somosomo, Taveuni, says preparations for the upcoming Commonwealth Games are going well as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal. Student of Fiji Agape Mission School, Maiwiriwiri says she began playing basketball at the age of 13.
item.content:encoded:
17-year-old Anastasia Maiwiriwiri of Somosomo, Taveuni, says preparations for the upcoming Commonwealth Games are going well as she prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal.

Student of Fiji Agape Mission School, Maiwiriwiri says she began playing basketball at the age of 13.

She says her aunt and uncle encouraged her to take up the sport, and their support has played an important role in her basketball journey.

Maiwiriwiri says she is excited about the Commonwealth Games, with the team working well together during training sessions.

She says the sessions have been productive and enjoyable as the team prepares for the competition.

Maiwiriwiri who will be competing in the Basketball 3x3 has encouraged aspiring athletes to keep pushing forward, remain disciplined and continue believing in themselves.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.

item.title: Fijian Drua fans set for another thrilling Super Rugby season with eight home games in 2027
item.description: Fijian Drua fans have plenty to look forward to, with the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua confirming that supporters can expect another action packed season in the Shop & Save Supermarket 2027 season, featuring eight home games. The announcement is sure to excite Drua faithful, who will once again be looking forward to filling the stands, creating an electric atmosphere and rallying behind their team a
item.content:encoded:
Fijian Drua fans have plenty to look forward to, with the Swire Shipping Fijian Drua confirming that supporters can expect another action packed season in the Shop & Save Supermarket 2027 season, featuring eight home games.

The announcement is sure to excite Drua faithful, who will once again be looking forward to filling the stands, creating an electric atmosphere and rallying behind their team as the side prepares for another big campaign.

With eight home games on the schedule, fans will have more opportunities to witness the Drua in action on home soil, as the team looks to deliver memorable performances and make the most of the home ground advantage.

For the passionate Drua supporters, the countdown to the 2027 season has already begun, with expectations building for another season filled with thrilling rugby, fierce competition and unforgettable moments.

The Drua will kick off their home campaign in Round 1 on February 13th against the Highlanders at Four R Stadium in Ba, with kick-off set for 3.30pm.

Their second home game will be played on February 27th against the Reds at HFC Bank Stadium in Suva, also at 3.30pm.

In Round 6, the Drua will travel to Churchill Park in Lautoka to face the Blues on March 20th, with kick-off scheduled for 3.30pm.

In Round 9, the Drua will host the Western Force at Four R Stadium in Ba on April 10th, with kick-off set for 4.30pm.

They will then welcome the Hurricanes to HFC Bank Stadium in Suva on April 30th.

In Round 14, the Drua will take on the Brumbies at Churchill Park in Lautoka on May 15th, with kick-off scheduled for 3.30pm. The following week, they will return to Suva to face the Crusaders at HFC Bank Stadium on May 21st.

The Drua’s final home game of the season will take place in Round 16 on May 29th, when they host the Waratahs at Four R Stadium in Ba. Kick-off is set for 4.30pm.

The Drua’s away games begin in Round 2 on February 20th when they face the Waratahs at Allianz Stadium in Sydney at 7.30pm.

Their second away game will be against the Brumbies on March 6 at GIO Stadium in Canberra, with kick-off at 7.30pm.

In Round 5, on March 13, they will take on the Hurricanes in Wellington at 4.30pm

According to the Drua, they will face the Reds in Round 7 on March 28 at Suncorp Stadium in Brisbane, with kick-off at 3.10pm and they will then play the Highlanders in Christchurch on Sunday, April 4th, at 2pm.

In Round 10, the Drua will meet the Chiefs on April 16 at FMG Stadium Waikato, with kick-off at 7.30pm and they will face the Blues at Eden Park in Auckland on May 7.

The Drua will round off their away fixtures against the Waratahs in Round 17 on June 4 in Perth, with kick-off at 8pm.

item.title: 17-year-old Tabete focused on mindset ahead of Youth Olympic Games
item.description: Maintaining the right mindset and persevering through challenges are among the biggest difficulties faced by 17-year-old Roko Ilaisa Tabete as he prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal. Tabete, who is from Yaroi in Matuku, Lau, will represent Fiji in triathalon.
item.content:encoded:
Maintaining the right mindset and persevering through challenges are among the biggest difficulties faced by 17-year-old Roko Ilaisa Tabete as he prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal.

Tabete, who is from Yaroi in Matuku, Lau, will represent Fiji in triathalon.

He says competing in track and field requires an individual mindset and the determination to keep going through difficult times.

The International School Suva student says he copes by singing songs in his head and talking to fellow athletes during training, as having people around him helps him improve.

Tabete says preparations for the Games are going well, with a focus on technical and physical training.

He says representing Fiji is both an honour and a privilege, having previously represented the country in track and field and basketball.

Tabete has thanked fans for their support and says he hopes to represent Fiji with pride at the Games.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.

item.title: Thomas Dunn returns to Bula FC for 2027 OFC Pro League season
item.description: Exciting news as Thomas Dunn will return to Extra Bula FC for the 2027 OFC Professional League season after helping the club finish third in the regular season and reach the Top Four playoffs in its inaugural campaign. Dunn says his first season in professional football helped improve his awareness of the game and deepen his understanding of football.
item.content:encoded:
Exciting news as Thomas Dunn will return to Extra Bula FC for the 2027 OFC Professional League season after helping the club finish third in the regular season and reach the Top Four playoffs in its inaugural campaign.

Dunn says his first season in professional football helped improve his awareness of the game and deepen his understanding of football.

He says he is looking forward to gaining more experience and making a greater contribution to the club next season.

Dunn also enjoyed success on the international stage, scoring the winning goal against Vanuatu in the 2026 MSG Prime Minister’s Cup final to help Fiji win the title after more than 20 years.

He says winning a title for his country was a special moment and something he had always dreamed of achieving.

Dunn says learning from experienced players, particularly Extra Bula FC and Fiji captain Roy Krishna, has helped him develop as a player and as a person, both on and off the field.

He says becoming a professional footballer was a long-held ambition and he is grateful to Extra Bula FC for giving him the opportunity to represent the club .

Dunn says his goals for the 2027 season are to improve on his performances from last season and score more goals.

He also acknowledged the support of his family, partner and daughter, saying being away from them is the biggest challenge of playing professional football.

Dunn says he makes the most of his breaks by spending time with his family.

He also expresses gratitude to the Bula Tribe for supporting the club throughout its inaugural season, saying the first season was only the beginning.
